rows.text: Ruric Thar taxes noncreature spells six life, and he taxes YOU too. The entire deck is built around that one fact: almost every card here is a creature, so his trigger is close to one-sided. Ramp is mana dorks, removal is creatures that fight, and card draw is creatures that draw. When you do run a noncreature spell it earns its slot, and you cast it before he lands or while you can afford the six.

rows.name: Ruric Thar, the Unbowed
rows.text: 6/6 reach and vigilance, must attack every combat, and every noncreature spell any player casts deals six to its caster. In a four-player pod that is twelve to eighteen damage a turn cycle that you did nothing to earn.

rows.name: Absorbing Man and Titania
rows.text: doubles all damage your CREATURE sources deal. Ruric Thar's trigger is a creature source, so every noncreature spell now costs them TWELVE. This is the single biggest upgrade in the deck.

rows.name: Dragonborn Champion
rows.text: draws a card whenever a source you control deals five or more damage to a player. Ruric Thar's six qualifies, so every spell they cast is a card for you.

rows.name: Rhythm of the Wild
rows.text: your creatures cannot be countered and they all get haste or a counter. It is the closest thing to a noncreature spell this deck is happy to cast.

rows.name: Scytheclaw Raptor
rows.text: four damage to anyone casting a spell on someone else's turn. Between this and Ruric Thar, instant-speed interaction costs ten.

rows.name: Adrenaline Jockey

rows.name: Magebane Lizard
rows.text: escalating damage for every noncreature spell in a turn, so combo turns are lethal to their pilot.

rows.name: Cindervines
rows.text: a ping per noncreature spell, and it sacrifices to destroy an artifact or enchantment and burn its controller.

rows.name: Shadow in the Warp
rows.text: two damage on their first noncreature spell each turn, and your first creature each turn costs two less.

rows.name: Heartwood Storyteller
rows.text: every noncreature spell any opponent casts draws each of their opponents a card. In a creature deck you are the player who benefits most.

rows.name: Combustion Man
rows.text: on every attack they either lose a permanent or take four.
Green creature decks lose to counterspells, so the deck simply removes that as an option.

rows.name: Frenzied Baloth

rows.name: Destiny Spinner
rows.text: creature and enchantment spells cannot be countered, and it animates a land as a finisher.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your whole board gets ward.

rows.name: Last March of the Ents
rows.text: cannot be countered, draws cards equal to your biggest toughness, and dumps your hand onto the battlefield.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a mana dork. Turn-one acceleration into a turn-three or four Ruric Thar is what makes the deck's tax matter before the table has set up.

Cast your noncreature spells BEFORE Ruric Thar, not after. Deploy Rhythm of the Wild, Shadow in the Warp and the auras early; once he is out, six life per noncreature spell is a real cost even for you.
Remember he attacks every combat whether you want him to or not. Plan around it — vigilance means he still blocks, but he will be tapped for the attack trigger of whoever you sent him at.

rows.name: Absorbing Man and Titania
rows.text: find it. Doubling Ruric Thar's trigger turns a slow tax into something the table cannot play through at all.
